summary:
The Pitcairn Islands stand under the United Kingdom's framework: defence and external affairs are reserved to the United Kingdom, and United Kingdom domestic measures such as the Equality Act 2010 and its 2025 single-sex-services code do not apply here of their own force. Local law governs, and those measures could reach Pitcairn only by Order in Council. Military service is likewise a United Kingdom responsibility rather than a local one.

Same-sex sexual activity has been legal in the Pitcairn Islands since 2001.

The Pitcairn Constitution Order 2010 prohibits discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation, and that guarantee has been in force since 2010.

Same-sex marriage has been legal since 14 May 2015. The Same Sex Marriage and Civil Partnerships Ordinance 2015 defines marriage as the union of two people regardless of sex, sexual orientation or gender identity. The Island Council approved the ordinance unanimously on 1 April 2015; Governor Jonathan Sinclair signed it on 5 May 2015 and it was published on 13 May 2015.

The same ordinance recognises civil partnerships performed outside Pitcairn. Adoption has been legal since 2015 and is open to married, unmarried and single people.

None of the roughly 50 residents is known to be in a same-sex relationship.
tangentialFactors:
Pitcairn's legal position on sexual orientation and gender identity mirrors the broader United Kingdom overseas-territory pattern, in which decriminalisation of same-sex activity and constitutional non-discrimination guarantees have spread across territories under the United Kingdom's authority since 2001.

The territory's tiny population of roughly 50 residents means that legal protections on paper sit alongside a social environment in which no resident is publicly known to be in a same-sex relationship, so the practical reach of the anti-discrimination guarantee is untested.
localsOnly:
Residents are protected against discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation under the Pitcairn Constitution Order 2010, in force since 2010.

Residents may marry a partner of the same sex under the Same Sex Marriage and Civil Partnerships Ordinance 2015, and the ordinance recognises civil partnerships solemnised outside Pitcairn.

Adoption is available to married, unmarried and single residents.

Defence and external affairs, including military service arrangements, are handled at United Kingdom level rather than locally.
outOfScopeNotes:
No source in the inventory addresses legal gender recognition, marker changes on documents, screening or medical gatekeeping, or access to gender-affirming care in the Pitcairn Islands; the position on these matters is unresolved on the present record.

No source addresses hate-crime provisions, enforcement of the constitutional non-discrimination guarantee, or any documented incident of violence against trans or gender-nonconforming people; these remain not sourced.

Entry, visa and border-screening rules for visitors are not covered by the inventory and are unresolved here.
